findings.evidence: Under the big light the paint looked better than ever, which was the cruelty of paint.
findings.diagnosis: Lands an aphoristic abstraction before any perception is established — interpretation-before-perception; the image is doing the work and the gloss steals it.

findings.evidence: It came out plain and sure, the way a thing does when it is right.
findings.diagnosis: The forbidden 'the way...' construction, double-telling: the line is already plain and sure, then the narrator moralizes the general case.

findings.evidence: His voice did a thing and came back level.
findings.diagnosis: Withholding the emotion is right, but 'did a thing' is a limp placeholder; a concrete catch would hold the same restraint.

findings.evidence: She wanted him to hear it.
findings.diagnosis: Names the intention the staged action already carries.
